시편-83-1.title: 시편 83장 1절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-1.exegesis: 8. As rightful sovereign of earth, God is invoked personally to correct the evils of His representatives.
시편-83-1.theologicalNote: 8. As rightful sovereign of earth, God is invoked personally to correct the evils of His representatives.

시편-83-2.title: 시편 83장 2절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-2.exegesis: PSALM 83 Psa 83:1-18 . Of Asaph--(See on Psa 74:1 , title). The historical occasion is probably that of 2Ch 20:1 , 2 (compare Psa 47:1-9; 48:1-14). After a general petition, the craft and rage of the combined enemies are described, God's former dealings recited, and a like summary and speedy destruction on them is invoked. 1. God addressed as indifferent (compare Psa 35:22 ; 39:12 ). be not still-- literally, "not quiet," as opposed to action.
시편-83-2.theologicalNote: PSALM 83 Psa 83:1-18 . Of Asaph--(See on Psa 74:1 , title). The historical occasion is probably that of 2Ch 20:1 , 2 (compare Psa 47:1-9; 48:1-14). 시편-83-4.title: 시편 83장 4절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-4.exegesis: 3. hidden ones-- whom God specially protects ( Psa 27:5 ; 91:1 ).

시편-83-5.title: 시편 83장 5절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-5.exegesis: 4. from being a nation-- utter destruction ( Is 7:8 ; 23:1 ). Israel-- here used for Judah, having been the common name.
시편-83-5.theologicalNote: 4. from being a nation-- utter destruction ( Is 7:8 ; 23:1 ). Israel-- here used for Judah, having been the common name.

시편-83-6.title: 시편 83장 6절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-6.exegesis: 5. they have consulted-- with heart, or cordially. together-- all alike.
시편-83-6.theologicalNote: 5. they have consulted-- with heart, or cordially. together-- all alike.

시편-83-10.title: 시편 83장 10절 역사문법적 주해
시편-83-10.exegesis: 9-11. Compare the similar fate of these ( 2Ch 20:23 ) with that of the foes mentioned in Jud 7:22 , here referred to. They destroyed one another (Jud 4:6-24; 7:25). Human remains form manure (compare 2Ki 9:37 ; Jr 9:22 ).

시편-83-17.exegesis: 16. that they may seek-- or as Psa 83:18 , supply "men," since Psa 83:17 , 18 amplify the sentiment of Psa 83:16 , expressing more fully the measure of destruction, and the lesson of God's being and perfections (compare 2Ch 20:29 ) taught to all men.
